$comment: Acceptance tests that describe behaviour we have NOT built yet.
The rule this file exists to serve, set by the Commander on 2026-08-09:
an acceptance test always describes CORRECT behaviour. If the behaviour is
not implemented, the test stays RED and says what should happen. It must
never be softened into a test that asserts what the code currently does.
We had done exactly that, and it is worse than having no test at all:
'should leave the Commander talking to himself: no assistant message ever
arrives' passed for weeks while Syl was unable to reply. It locked in the
defect, had to be rewritten rather than deleted, and made a green suite
claim the story worked.
HOW THE GATE USES THIS FILE — strict in BOTH directions:
- a failure NOT listed here breaks the build. The ordinary gate, kept.
- a test listed here that PASSES breaks the build too, demanding that it
be promoted out of this file. Without that half the list rots: entries
linger long after the feature lands, and someone eventually deletes a
stale line together with real coverage.
- a listed test that no longer EXISTS breaks the build, so a rename
cannot quietly retire a requirement.
Every entry needs a bead, so 'expected failure' always means tracked work
and never 'known broken, nobody's problem'.
Deliberately NOT using vitest's `it.fails`. It reports a green tick under
the correct-behaviour name, which reads as 'that feature works' to anyone
scanning CI — and it passes when the test fails for ANY reason, including
a typo or a bad import. That is the meaningless-green problem it was
supposed to solve, wearing a different hat.

expected.test: holographic query kernels — behaviour reason should rank the fact matching ALL entities above facts matching one, by a margin above the noise floor
expected.why: reason() is documented upstream as compositional retrieval no embedding DB can do. It does not discriminate: every fact scores 0.489-0.491, a spread of 0.002, which is the noise floor. Verified digit-for-digit against the Python original on the same corpus, so this is an inherited defect and not a porting error. Root cause: bundle() is a circular mean, which discards the magnitude that classic HRR unbinding needs to recover a composed vector. related() on the same data separates by 0.30 and works.

expected.test: holographic query kernels — behaviour reason should rank a fact that contains the queried entity above one that does not
expected.why: Same defect, stated at its starkest: for reason(['Grace']) the fact WITHOUT Grace scores 0.5042 and the fact WITH Grace scores 0.4797. The ranking is not merely weak, it is inverted.

expected.test: holographic query kernels — behaviour probe should rank facts whose entity slot holds the probe above one that does not
expected.why: Same defect in probe(): the fact whose entity is Grace ranks FIRST for probe('Ada'), ahead of both facts that actually carry Ada. related() and contradict() are the two kernels that work today; the nightly sweep (syl-005.4.2) must use those and not these.

expected.test: deploy — a rollback after a migration should restore the schema the restored build expects
expected.why: A health-gated rollback restores the CODE and leaves the SCHEMA forward. Migrations run on the way up and there is no down path, so after a failed deploy the restored build runs against a database it has never seen. Additive migrations usually survive that and a destructive one does not, and nothing today tells the two apart. The deploy reports the migrations involved and reports schemaRestored: false rather than pretending — but 'the code is back' and 'the system is back' are different claims, and only the first is true. Fixing it needs either down-migrations or a snapshot of the SQLite file taken before the deploy.

expected.test: she forms connections — the five bars for digestion (syl-zdf) should connect a person to another person by a typed relation
expected.why: The dandelion, stated as a test. Measured on the live graph 2026-08-11: 30 nodes, 29 edges, every one relation='stated' provenance from a single hub, and ZERO edges between two real memories. Not 'an edge exists' -- 29 of those exist and they are all the same edge. This asks for a TYPED edge between two real memories, which nothing has ever written.

expected.test: she forms connections — the five bars for digestion (syl-zdf) should resolve two mentions of one person to one identity, without merging two people
expected.why: memory_nodes.subject_id exists and extract-apply.ts:404 says 'Deliberately no subjectId', so it has never been populated on the conversational path. Live consequence: 'Ela' and 'Ela — his wife' are two person nodes for one woman, and the newer duplicate EVICTED the richer one from working memory. Deliberately agnostic about whether resolution merges rows or shares an identity across them -- only 'two people who are the same person' is wrong.

expected.test: she forms connections — the five bars for digestion (syl-zdf) should never evict a person or a goal in favour of a more recent fact
expected.why: Measured at the old 4,000-byte budget: 23 admitted, 7 dropped, and the seven were his own name, his wife, his son, his daughter, where he lives, his job title and what his company does. Uncle Bob survived because he was more recent. Asserted at a tight budget rather than the production one so it tests the eviction RULE, which is what has to hold when the graph is large and the budget binds again.

expected.test: she forms connections — the five bars for digestion (syl-zdf) should rank memories by something that actually varies
expected.why: SALIENCE_SQL sums incident hot-edge weights. Measured distribution on the live graph: the hub scored 29 and EVERY other node scored exactly 1. A constant primary sort key is not a sort key -- admission falls through to the recency tiebreaker, which is the direct cause of the eviction above.

expected.test: she forms connections — the five bars for digestion (syl-zdf) should insert at least one inferred edge that survives a night
expected.why: dream_sessions has zero rows: the job was wired to a clock on 2026-08-10 and its only run was correctly skipped as outside the window, so this is a claim syl-005.4 made and never evidenced. Measured cause, by running the real kernels against the real graph: related() proposes 0 candidates because entitiesOf() derives probes from edges and every node's only edge is provenance, so all 30 yield the same constant probe. contradict() proposes 0 -- the whole graph scores 0.180-0.291 against a 0.300 threshold. The dream cannot bootstrap itself out of a dandelion, which is why digestion comes first.
